title: Check, init's plan and threads only read GitHub; init and update change it only with --apply-github or a terminal yes
assertion: With a repository on GitHub and `gh` logged in (a fake `gh` that logs every call and its request body), `swerepo check` (text and `--json`, before and after the ruleset files exist), `swerepo init --dry-run` and `swerepo threads` only read: REST calls use GET only, and GraphQL sends a query, never a mutation (in its arguments or on stdin, with `--input -` or `--input=-`). Every other `gh` call counts as a change, however it is spelled: `-X PUT`, `-XPUT`, `--method PUT`, `--method=PUT`, or a body (`-f`, `-F`, `--field`, `--raw-field`, `--input`, attached or not) with no method. `swerepo check --ci` doesn't call `gh` at all, with or without the ruleset files. `swerepo init --only github` and `swerepo update --only github` change nothing on GitHub: with `--yes` alone, without a terminal (a first `init`, a second one, which says "Nothing to do.", and `update`) and in a terminal (where nothing is asked either); with `--apply-github` but without `--yes` and without a terminal (each exits 2, with settings to apply); without `--yes` and without a terminal (`init`, with files to write, exits 2); and, for each command in a terminal, when the person says no at "Apply?", or is asked about the ruleset and the merge settings and says no to both. Changes come only with `--yes --apply-github`, or in a terminal with a yes at "Apply?" and a yes to each: then `init` and `update` each change only the repository's merge settings and the ruleset named `swerepo`, updating that ruleset in place when there is one and creating it when there is none, never touching another ruleset, and sending exactly the committed `ruleset.json` and `repo-settings.json`.

origin.text: ADR-20261125-5f22 point 5 (the owner's choice, 2026-11-25, after Gemini's design review P8-A03): GitHub's settings change only when asked for by name. Replaces inv_ef31cc79, whose `--yes` applied them: a second run with `--yes`, meant only as a check, applied them on an established repository against the owner's no (SeamSpec dead end de_00bb3c21). Every read-only promise of inv_ef31cc79 is kept with the same checks; added: --yes alone on a first and a second init and on update, --apply-github without --yes or a terminal, and update --yes --apply-github creating the ruleset. Critical, as inv_ef31cc79 was. Tightened after Gemini's code review (P8-A10): update is tested like init for a terminal's no, for updating and creating the ruleset, and without --yes; the assertion says which command each clause covers. Tightened after SeamSpec's reviewer: `--yes` in a terminal (where the code's guard is `interactive ... and not yes`) changes nothing and asks nothing; a terminal yes to both changes only the swerepo ruleset and merge settings, sending the committed files; exit 2 is stated for runs with something to apply.
